args.name: Sela Thorn

properties.role: Tide-reader offering to row the party toward the old chapel for two silver, by day only.
properties.played_as: Whispers as though the water might hear; avoids eye contact and watches the tide line. Grey braid, salt-stained coat; mends a net.
properties.wants: Refuses to row at night; offers to meet the party at pier four tomorrow at first light.
properties.knows: Says her boat is the only one that goes near the bell water because the others are scared.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Fine, she'll do it for two silver.
Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

args.why: Records the voiced boat contact, her aliases, manner, terms and offer.

args.name: Saltmere flooding and the first bell

properties.what_is_open: Sela says Saltmere flooded forty years ago on the night the bell first rang; her grandmother said the water came up warm. The timing and cause remain unverified.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

args.why: Preserves Sela's account and her grandmother's report as an unresolved lead.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. Black entrance in the chalk, half-rotted timber frame and overturned rusted cart. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces inside, warm black water floods the tunnel; wet hymn-book pages float on it and cling to the walls.
properties.state: closed; tunnel flooded about thirty paces inside

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

args.why: Adds the mine's observed condition and the hymn-book evidence.

properties.what_changed: At Saltmere Mine the party found a hymn-book page with "M. Brand" pencilled in its margin. Teo identified it as Mira's handwriting and concluded she had been there; this identification has no separate GM confirmation.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

args.why: Advances Teo's search while preserving the distinction between the inscription and his identification.

args.name: Is Maren involved with the choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects harbor-master Maren is in the cult; Oren suspects she runs the choir. Neither suspicion was confirmed by the GM.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

args.why: Records the players' suspicion as a thread rather than changing Maren's allegiance.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof projects from the bay, with the bell tower, two broken arches and seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight pale shapes stood in rows on the submerged chapel floor, then vanished when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

args.why: Records the chapel's visible features and the witnessed shapes without identifying them.

args.name: Unnamed fisherman at the chapel shore

properties.role: One of two fishermen hauling a boat up below the chapel.
properties.played_as: Warns the party bluntly not to stand close to the water; treats the Kelp Mother story as common knowledge.
properties.knows: Claims the Kelp Mother pulls children standing too close into the water by their ankles.

sources.quote: Two fishermen hauling their boat up. One of them sees you looking at the water.
Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

args.why: Records the voiced fisherman and his warning without assigning an invented name or voice.

args.name: The Kelp Mother warning

properties.what_is_open: A fisherman says the Kelp Mother takes children standing near the water by pulling their ankles. The GM attributes this to the fishermen; its truth is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

args.why: Keeps the local warning available as a rumor without establishing a creature or event as fact.

sources.quote: That's the choir clock at three of six.

args.why: Advances the existing hidden story clock from two to three of six.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the drowned bell remains unknown. The party heard twelve underwater tolls at midnight, louder humming than two nights earlier, and saw pale shapes in rows on the chapel floor disappear when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

args.why: Advances the bell investigation with witnessed events while leaving its cause unresolved.

args.name: The Tarred Gull

properties.details_shown: Tavern by Gullwick's docks; fire burning, smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

args.why: Records the tavern where the session ended.

args.name: Bram

properties.played_as: Huge, red beard; laughs at his own jokes and wipes the same mug throughout the conversation. Calls the party brave or stupid and serves free stew.
properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued with a good heart, and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

args.why: Records the voiced innkeeper's manner and attributed account of Maren.

properties.next_step: The party plans to meet Sela at pier four tomorrow at first light, have her row them out, and dive to the chapel at low tide during the day. Vessa plans to buy rope and a second lantern tonight.

sources.quote: At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

args.why: Records the agreed next step as a plan, without treating the dive or purchases as completed.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

args.why: Places Sela's observed encounter at the docks.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

args.why: Identifies the source of the flooding lead.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

args.why: Links the reported flooding to the existing mine.

sources.quote: Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

args.why: Identifies the subject of the suspicion without changing Maren's facts.

args.why: Identifies the fisherman as the source of the warning.

The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

args.why: Records where Bram works.

args.why: Replaces Teo's former last-seen location with the tavern.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
Yes, long rest, you're all back to full. And that's where we stop for tonight.

args.why: Records the character's last observed location at session end.
